title: legal-redlines-scratchpad-ethan-kim
content:
Legal redlines scratchpad - Ethan Kim

Context:
- Working draft notes for sales/legal on typical customer contract redlines. Mostly for Dedicated/Private deals but applicable to hosted when customers push on data/ML IP.
- Quick reference for clauses that commonly get redlined and the trade-offs we accept. Not final - iterate with Olivia (legal) + Liam (security) on high-risk deals.

Key clauses to watch (high priority):
1) Data processing / ownership / ML improvements
   - Redline: Customer wants all outputs and derived models to be customer-owned.
   - Risk: Prevents us from using telemetry to improve service; legal/regulatory exposure if we claim rights over customer PII.
   - Talking points: ask for "Customer Data" ownership; grant Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, anonymized, aggregated usage right for product improvement with opt-out for regulated customers. Add strict de-id / no-PII language.
   - Fallback: If customer insists on full ownership, carve out: aggregated telemetry + service-quality metrics only; no model weights or retraining on raw customer data.

2) Security / compliance commitments (SOC2, encryption, KMS)
   - Redline: Customer requires SOC2 Type II and specific encryption-at-rest keys + HSM.
   - Risk: Operational/expense impact for Private deals; for Hosted we can offer KMS integration for Enterprise plan.
   - Talking points: commit to SOC2 Type II within X days for Private installs OR provide current report and roadmap. Offer customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private.
   - Fallback: For new customers, 90-day remediation plan + temporary additional controls (VPC peering, IP allowlist).

3) Liability cap and indemnity
   - Redline: Unlimited liability / punitive damages / unlimited data breach liability.
   - Risk: Financial exposure.
   - Talking points: standard limitation of liability = greater of (fees paid in prior 12 months) or $1M (or propose 3x fees up to $3M). Carve-outs: breach of confidentiality, IP infringement, gross negligence (mutual). No punitive damages.
   - Negotiation position: Prefer mutual indemnity for third-party IP claims and data breaches caused by each party. If customer insists on higher cap, ask for higher commercial commitment (longer term / higher minimums).

4) Service levels / service credits / uptime
   - Redline: SLA with steep credits and availability penalty (e.g., 99.99% uptime, credits >50% fees).
   - Risk: Unclear definitions of downtime for model degradation/throughput.
   - Talking points: Define SLOs clearly (request/response, median p50/p99 latency, and availability for control plane). Cap credits at a percentage of monthly fees (e.g., max 25%). Exclude outages caused by customer misuse or third-party infra.

5) Audit & compliance rights / access to infra logs
   - Redline: Unlimited audit rights + live access to logs and root cause diagnostic.
   - Risk: Security exposure and operational burden.
   - Talking points: Offer annual audits or SOC2 report + scoped security questionnaire (SIG). For Dedicated/Private, allow scheduled on-site or remote audits with 30 days notice and NDA. Limit frequency and scope.

6) Termination and transition / data return & deletion
   - Redline: Customer asks for immediate deletion and full data export with 7-day turnaround.
   - Risk: Operational feasibility and forensics needs.
   - Talking points: Commit to data export within 30 days (configurable) and deletion within 90 days post-termination, with exception for backups and legal holds. Provide documented transition plan and egress formats.

7) Export controls / restricted tech use / export classification
   - Redline: Customer wants explicit guarantees we won't run models with certain outputs or on certain jurisdictions.
   - Talking points: Affirm compliance with applicable export laws; offer region/cluster restrictions for Private and Dedicated. For hosted, provide region-level routing and data residency guarantees where available.

8) Confidentiality / injunctive relief
   - Redline: Broad confidentiality definitions and unilateral injunctive relief.
   - Talking points: Mutual confidentiality with defined categories; preserve injunctive relief for IP/PII breaches only.

9) Subprocessors / third parties / subcontractors
   - Redline: Customer wants to approve every subprocessor.
   - Talking points: Provide a subprocessors list and commit to notice before changes + objection path. For infra-level (cloud provider) carve out standard list.

10) Governing law / jurisdiction
    - Redline: Customer picks their local jurisdiction (non-US).
    - Talking points: Try to keep commercial agreements in CA or NY; accept EEA local law for regulated customers with sales/legal sign-off. Consider arbitration vs. court.

Special notes for ML-specific clauses:
- Model weights & fine-tuning: customers ask we not use their fine-tuned models. We should offer an option: private model isolation (Dedicated/Private) vs hosted where we only use anonymized aggregate metrics.
- Output liability: customers want guarantees about hallucinations. We must limit liability and provide best-effort mitigation (prompt templates, guardrails, safety filters) but no warranty of factual accuracy.
- Benchmarking / performance claims: ensure any performance SLAs are scoped to test sets and not general usage.

Negotiation playbook / talking points (short):
- Always start with mutual language (mutual indemnity, mutual confidentiality).
- Data ownership: customer owns raw customer data; Redwood gets limited anonymized usage for improvements unless otherwise negotiated.
- Cap liability to fees or set dollar cap; carve-outs for IP and confidentiality.
- Provide SOC2 report; offer KMS for enterprise.
- Limit audit frequency and scope; provide SOC2 + SIG questionnaire.
- Transition assistance with defined timelines; avoid immediate deletion demands that impede investigations.

Quick fallback values (for quick replies during redline calls):
- Liability cap: greater of fees in prior 12 months or $1,000,000 (negotiate up depending on ARR).
- Indemnity: mutual for third-party IP and direct damages from breach.
- Data retention on terminate: export within 30 days; deletion within 90 days (backups exception).
- SLA credits: cap at 25% monthly fees; availability definition and exclusions required.

Open questions / items to escalate to Olivia (legal) or Liam (security):
- When to accept customer request for exclusive ownership of derived models? (Escalate - only if significant ARR + legal carveout for anonymization).
- What is minimum SOC2 remediation timeline acceptable?
- Approval threshold for increasing liability cap vs commercial concessions.

Stakeholders to loop in per deal:
- Legal: Olivia Wright (final sign-off on any deviation)
- Security/Infra: Liam Brown (technical feasibility for KMS, VPC peering, audit access)
- Sales: Ava Chen (commercial trade-offs)
- Solutions Eng: Noah Anderson (impact on runbook, SLOs, onboarding)

Notes to self / negotiation checklist:
- Read customer DPA and compare to Redwood template. Flag: data use for model improvement + anonymization protections.
- Confirm customer's required data residency region and if Private/Dedicated is required.
- Ask for sample legal language they want for ownership; propose our standard phrasing.
- If customer requests audit, propose SOC2 + annual 3rd-party audit in lieu of ad hoc logs access.

References / templates:
- Internal DPA template: CONF-2482 (linked above)
- Redwood standard SLA & liability language: JIRA-INFR-1123
- Old negotiated deal examples: see sales folder / deals/2025-Q3/enterprise-acme (ask Ava)

Last quick tips for calls:
- Keep it simple: use mutual language and highlight protections for customer data.
- Trade technical concessions for higher MRR / longer term commitments.
- Escalate early to Olivia on any unlimited liability or exclusive ownership asks.

End of scratchpad.
summary: Personal redline notes for contract negotiation: data ownership, liability, SLA, security, audit rights, and ML-specific clauses. Use mutual language; protect product-improvement rights; demand SOC2 or roadmap; limit liability; provide clear SLAs and transition timelines. Escalate to Olivia/Liam for high-risk asks.
